emblem.latin_monogram: WH: an intertwined cursive capital W and a cursive capital H. The H is a looped script form (an upright stroke joined to a C-like bowl), so at this resolution it could also be taken as 'C'. W is clear.
emblem.hebrew_reading: וואלף ב[?]ל[?]א[?]ו[?] [?]  א״[?]  ה[?]יי[?]ד[?][?]ם[?]  (the legend runs right to left, starting at lower right and going up and over the top. Only the first word, וואלף, can be read with confidence. The rest seems to repeat the letter shapes of the signature in image 2, but individual letters cannot be fixed at this resolution.)
letter_evidence: Lower right, rotated along the oval: two short upright strokes = וו; then a small א with a slanted middle stroke and two legs; then a tall looped ascender = ל; then a downstroke with a looped head that drops below the line = final ף. Reading: וואלף. Fairly confident.

Right side, going up: a '3'-shaped letter with a small mark above it, read as ב with an overstroke (possibly an abbreviation mark or decoration), linked to a large looped flourish. Same shape as the signature's second word.

Upper right: a cluster of looped tall strokes with an א-like letter between them, ending in a tall bracket-like vertical stroke. The same letter shapes appear in the signature's third word. Possibly ל…א…ו, but the letters are not distinct.
Top: a large Z-shaped capital-style letter with a small '2'-like letter tucked under its top bar. Matches the large letter in the signature. Not identified.
Top left: א followed by a double geresh-like mark (״) and a looped letter, i.e. an abbreviation written א״ plus a letter. The final letter is unclear.
Upper left: three small cursive letters (n-like shapes), perhaps ה/י/ד, then a tall swooping letter (a large C/N-shaped stroke).
Lower left: a small letter with two raised strokes (״) and a closing '3'-shaped letter, possibly ס/ם written cursively. Unclear.
Decorative, not letters: the inner and outer oval rules, the large entry and exit swashes on the tall letters, and the hairline tails.
uncertainties: Only וואלף is read with reasonable confidence. Every other letter is tentative or unidentified and is marked [?].
The mark above the ב-like letter may be an abbreviation sign, a supralinear letter, or decoration.
The Z-shaped letter and the small '2' inside it are not identified. The pair could be one letter with an ornament, or a letter plus a superscript.
I could not tell which ״ marks are gershayim (abbreviation marks) and which are small yods.
The resolution is too low to count the strokes in the small cursive clusters with confidence.
I did not expand any abbreviation or supply any name.

signature.reading: וואלף בׄ[?]ל[?] [?]א[?]ו[?]ן[?] [?] א״[?] ה״יד[?] [?]יי[?]ם[?]  (right to left. Only וואלף is secure. The other groups are given as letter-shape inventories, not as words.)
letter_evidence: Word 1 (far right): two plain vertical strokes = וו; a small slanted א; a tall looped ascender = ל; a heavy downstroke under a loop that ends below the baseline in a small knob = final ף. Reading: וואלף.

Word 2: a '3'-shaped cursive letter, read as ב (cursive form), with a short hooked mark above it (a small ל-like or apostrophe-like stroke). Its tail runs into a long sweep below the line that ends in a tall loop on the left. The tall loop may be a ל ascender (giving ב…ל) or only an exit flourish. The heart-shaped curl under the '3' is decorative.

Word 3: from right, a looped ascender (ל?), a small א, another looped ascender (ל?) or a ו, then a tall curved vertical stroke on the left like a bracket, possibly ן or a long ו. The middle shape is clearly א. The others are uncertain.
Word 4: a large letter with a Z-shaped top bar and a loop, a small '2'-like letter under the bar, and a huge open loop below the line. Not identified. Most of the loop below the line is flourish.

Word 5: a small א followed by a raised double stroke (״, which may be gershayim or two small yods). Under and to the left of it is a large C-shaped swash. The swash is probably decorative, or else the tail of a letter.

Word 6 (left): a small ה, a raised double stroke (״), a small ד, then a large looping letter with a small ר/י-like mark above it (perhaps נ or ה with an overstroke), then small strokes like יי and a closing letter shaped like ס or ם. The long underline loop that wraps under this word is decorative.
uncertainties: Apart from וואלף, no word is read with confidence. Letters are listed by visible shape only.
It is unclear whether the long swashes in words 2 and 4 contain letters (ן, ל) or are pure ornament.
The marks above letters in words 2 and 6 may be abbreviation signs, superscript letters, or decoration.
The ״ marks in words 5 and 6 could be abbreviation marks or pairs of yods. This changes whether the words are abbreviations.
The last letter (ס-shaped) may be ם or ס. A small trailing stroke may be ן or only an exit tail.
The emblem legend seems to repeat the same sequence, but neither image clears up the other's doubtful letters.
I did not expand any abbreviation or supply any name from memory.

Line 4, first word: the third letter looks like נ (מונה) in this scan, but at this size נ and ג look very alike, and the usual formula is מוגה ומסודר. The visible form is recorded and the letter is uncertain.
The abbreviations ע״י, תשכ״ה and לפ״ק are transcribed as printed, with gershayim, and not expanded.

Faint mirror-image text from the other side of the leaf shows through: English lines near 'עם תרגום אנגלי' (something like 'Pentateuch … ') and near 'רבקה מארמארשטיין' (something like 'Volume I: … the New …'). There is also a faint round seal or emblem behind the signature. These are not part of this page's text and are too faint to read reliably.
Spelling as printed: מארמארשטיין, גאלדשמידט, באזעל.
